verdict: Sound for the current HSConfig architecture. The model stays slim and autonomous because runtime permission is tied to load-safe technical package validity in reports/operator_summary.json, while weak source depth, unsupported claims, partial mechanics, warning-only mechanics, source-informed debt, and diagnostic contract-spine details remain visible as reports or warnings. The current implementation avoids blocking valid load-safe packages and does not create an extra approval gate, as long as future work preserves the single-gate boundary.

current_strengths: The architecture has one normal runtime gate. The apply gate reads reports/operator_summary.json and validates package structure; it does not read source-contract audit reports, acceptance matrix diagnostics, claim lifecycle rows, or contract spine rows as independent permission sources.

Source strength is separated from runtime load safety. SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG means high-confidence source closure, while VALID_BUT_NOT_GUIDE_STRONG, STATIC_SEMANTICS_USABLE, load_safe_but_thin, and READY_TO_APPLY_WITH_WARNINGS can still describe valid packages that are safe to apply with visible follow-up work.

Weak source depth stays actionable. Source-claim gaps are converted into source_depth_lane, first_missing_link, recommended_next_claim_kind, and recommended_next_source_action, so the operator gets a repair path without stopping a valid package.

Unsupported and low-confidence source claims do not disappear and do not become hidden blockers. They are represented as unsupported, suppressed, report-only, generic-low-confidence, or contract-gap rows with reasons.

Mechanic handling is intentionally narrow. Direct mechanics can lower to documented surfaces, identity-gated mechanics lower only with exact identity, partial mechanics emit only safe posture or CardID fragments, and warning-only mechanics remain report-only.

The model does not invent runtime behavior for unsupported mechanics. Unknown future mechanics and warning-only mechanics receive report-only lowering policies with no allowed runtime blocks or default runtime blocks.

No-block failure modes are operator-readable. technical_hard_block is the only hard-stop category, while source depth, mechanic visibility, drift, guide-strength gaps, combo uncertainty, and runtime-evidence-only tuning are explanatory categories.

The any-deck claim is tested through a real deck matrix rather than just unit-level mocks. The matrix covers twelve valid Wild deck inputs and asserts load-safe package shape, operator summaries, required runtime files, CardID rich output, and diagnostic non-blocking status.

Start-of-game and hero-power-transform semantics are kept out of opening-hand mulligan logic unless there is separate explicit mulligan evidence, which preserves effect semantics without over-blocking or over-lowering.
Legacy or optional surfaces stay outside the normal path. Presume.json and Concede.json are blocked in normal apply output, which keeps the runtime package slim and avoids broadening the gate.
gaps_or_risks: The any-valid-deck no-block promise is still enforced through representative decks, package-shape rules, and mechanic buckets rather than exhaustive proof over every possible future deck, card, and keyword. Future Hearthstone mechanics can still create new warning-only or drift rows that need registry updates.

The source contract policy is distributed across several modules: source_document_model.py, source_contract_matrix.py, source_contract_conformance.py, builders, routers, summaries, and tests. A new claim kind or runtime surface can regress if those update points are not changed together.

The diagnostic layer is useful but broad. Source contract audit, conformance, source-to-runtime explainability, source claim gap, mechanic drift, and operator projections must keep projecting the same contract rather than growing into parallel business logic.

Diagnostic attribution can become less precise if builders stop carrying explicit claim_id or claim_refs. The audit has fallback logic, but exact claim provenance is stronger and should remain preferred.

Thin but valid packages are expected. Some decks with weak guide evidence, warning-only mechanics, partial mechanics, or combo uncertainty will apply safely but may be strategically shallow until source gaps are closed.

Gate creep remains the main architectural failure mode. If future code lets source_contract_audit.json, source_to_runtime_explainability.json, acceptance-matrix output, or contract_spine_rows deny or grant runtime writes, the model would no longer be slim or autonomous.

Operator wording has to remain precise. If documentation or CLI output starts implying that SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG is required for runtime apply, or that ALLOWED_WITH_WARNINGS needs a second approval step, it would conflict with the current no-block contract.

Warning-only mechanics must stay visible enough to act on. If the reports become too terse, the system could technically remain non-blocking while leaving the operator without a clear next source or mechanic action.
recommended_next_actions: No immediate gate change is needed. Preserve the current single-gate model: reports/operator_summary.json plus structural package validation decide runtime apply, while source-contract diagnostics remain explanatory.

Keep the focused guard tests in the normal verification set for this area: test_apply_gate.py, test_no_second_gate_contract.py, test_apply_authority_boundary.py, test_operator_guidance.py, test_mechanic_support.py, test_source_claim_quality_autonomy.py, and test_universal_wild_no_block_matrix.py.

When adding a new claim kind, update the supported claim-kind set, source contract matrix, surface gate, conformance expectations, builder or router behavior, source gap recommendation mapping, and tests in one small contract change.

When adding or reclassifying a mechanic, update mechanic_support.py with an explicit direct, identity_gated_direct, partial, or warning_only boundary and add tests proving whether it may emit runtime rows or must stay report-only.

Keep weak-source improvements as report-quality work, not gate work. Improve source_claim_gap_report.json, guide_source_depth_report.json, and operator guidance when source depth is weak, but do not require a second approval step for load-safe packages.

Prefer adding narrow regression tests for real drift cases over broadening runtime surfaces. New runtime lowering should require documented VisionAI surface support and exact source-backed identity or sequence evidence.
Retain the representative no-block matrix and supplement it only when a new deck family proves a genuinely missing source-depth or mechanic boundary that current fixtures do not exercise.
no_blocking_constraints: Do not block a package only because semantic_status is VALID_BUT_NOT_GUIDE_STRONG, STATIC_SEMANTICS_USABLE, NEEDS_MORE_RESEARCH, or because config_usefulness is load_safe_but_thin, if the package is technically valid and runtime_apply_mode is load_safe_apply.
Keep SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG as a source-confidence and handoff label, not the runtime-write gate.
Keep apply permission tied to reports/operator_summary.json, technical_status=VALID_PACKAGE, runtime_apply_mode=load_safe_apply, runtime_apply_allowed=true, and apply_gate structural validation.

Treat missing guide claims, generic-low-confidence cards, weak source evidence, source-depth warnings, source-informed debt, runtime-surface gaps, combo uncertainty, partial mechanics, warning-only mechanics, and mechanic drift as visible follow-up work rather than apply blockers.

Block only true technical or load-safety failures: malformed or unsupported deck input, invalid JSON, missing reports/operator_summary.json, missing reports/input_manifest.json, missing CustomConfig runtime directory, missing GlobalValues.json or Mulligan.json, undeclared or missing generated runtime files, nested runtime files, invalid runtime JSON, normal-path Presume.json or Concede.json, forged or stale apply evidence, or unsupported VisionAI filenames or blocks.

Do not let source_contract_audit.json, source_to_runtime_explainability.json, source_contract_conformance output, contract_spine_rows, claim_lifecycle_rows, acceptance-matrix diagnostics, or source_informed_apply_readiness become independent runtime-write gates.

Do not add a new expert flag or approval prompt for ordinary load_safe_apply packages. The legacy --allow-source-informed concept must remain backward-compatible and diagnostic-only rather than a normal apply requirement.

Do not invent runtime rows for unsupported, warning-only, or identity-unresolved mechanics. Suppress them with reasons, report them in mechanic visibility or source gap outputs, and keep the package load-safe.

Do not infer opening-hand mulligan keeps from card importance, start-of-game effects, deckbuilding effects, hero-power-transform text, or broad gameplan prose. Require explicit mulligan_keep or mulligan_discard evidence for Mulligan.json.
Keep post-game tuning, replay evidence, winrate claims, and runtime performance evaluation outside HSConfig's pre-run source-contract gate; those belong to the separate post-run tuning workflow.
